name: Every ranked briefing row states where the nearest wall on the OTHER side of price sits
notes: Re-verified goal-desk-iter-19 by browser-qa-agent (2026-07-29). Iter-19 corrected _select_opposite_band's tie-break to distance-first (goal.md J-14 step 1 verbatim), fixing iter-18's shipped class-first bug on 2 of 63 real rows (HONA, META). This is a backend-only fix (desk_screen.py); zero page.tsx diff.

The legacy-pin steps below are UNCHANGED and still durable: screen-2026-06-22-3ecd45c062c7 predates the opposite_band field entirely (recorded iter-3, before iter-18 shipped it), so every one of its rows permanently reads the fallback 'opposite wall not recorded in this snapshot' under the append-only rail -- confirmed again this run by clicking that exact history row and reading the AAPL row's opposite cell verbatim. This assertion is unaffected by iter-19's selection-rule change (it only touches which band is selected on NEW rows, never legacy ones) and remains the most future-proof anchor for this journey's regression replay.

The POPULATED, corrected-rule case was independently verified this run LIVE against the running rig's own real ambient data (backend :8301 / frontend :3301, apps/backend/.data) -- no separate fixture-scoped rig was needed because the ambient store already held a freshly-computed real screen (screen-2026-07-20-ca185294a384, 100 ranked rows, recorded 2026-07-29T12:24:33Z, i.e. after this iteration's fix landed). Definitive proof the corrected distance-first rule is live: HONA's row (resistance Class A, close 211.63) has support candidates including class A bands ~266bps and ~351bps away AND a class B band at 210.23-211.63 touching price at 0.00 bps (cross-checked via GET /research/tradability?symbol=HONA&as_of=2026-07-20T23:59:59Z) -- the rendered opposite cell reads 'opposite support B 210.23-211.63 . 0.00 bps', the class-B/nearest band, which the OLD class-first rule could never have selected over the nearer-ranking class A candidates. A near (<=25bps) and far (>1000bps) row pair (BRK-B 1.22bps / UBER 1.38bps / MDT 2.40bps all near; DIS 1128.29bps far) were legible together in one screenshot at the very top of the ranked table with zero scrolling needed -- reports/qa/goal-desk-iter-19-evidence/J-14-opposite-near-far.png. The bands_by_class tooltip content was confirmed correct via direct DOM attribute inspection of the row's title attribute (e.g. 'bands by class A 10 . B 0 . C 0 . unclassified 0') but a VISUAL screenshot of it could not be captured: the tooltip is a native HTML title attribute (apps/frontend/app/desk/page.tsx:346, deskRowDrillInTitle), and native title tooltips do not render into headless Chrome's CDP screenshot surface -- confirmed by two independent hover+screenshot attempts this run (reports/qa/goal-desk-iter-19-evidence/J-14-tooltip-hover-attempt.png shows no visible popup despite a correct title attribute underneath) and consistent with the same-day functional-QA agent's own earlier attempt (reports/qa/goal-desk-iter-19-evidence/UT-04-tooltip.png, also no visible popup). This is a headless-browser environment limitation, not a product defect.
This script clicks a Screen History row, which is SAFE to replay repeatedly: selecting a row only drives GET /research/desk/screen?id=<id>, a plain read that recomputes nothing and writes nothing.
